title: Claude Certified Associate – Foundations
description: Claude Certified Associate – Foundations practice questions, extracted from Claude Certified Associate – Foundations.pdf.

questions.question: You are a knowledge worker deciding whether to escalate a Claude-generated output. Which is the correct order of decision steps? 1. Identify the audience and the impact of the output if it is wrong. 2. Document the decision and the rationale for traceability. 3. Compare the output's risk profile to the organization's escalation criteria. 4. Decide whether to use, iterate further, or escalate. 5. Assess the output's accuracy, completeness, and any unverified claims.
You are writing system-level instructions for a Project that supports recurring writing tasks. Which step should be performed first when writing the system-level instructions?

options.text: Distribute the finalized instructions to collaborators on the Project.
Define the purpose of the Project and the boundaries the instructions must respect.
Refine the drafted instructions based on observed gaps from validation runs.
Validate the drafted instructions against representative requests for the Project.

questions.question: A knowledge worker is explaining how to use feedback to improve Claude-supported work over time. Which description is most accurate?

options.text: Capture feedback only after several runs so patterns emerge from the volume of observations, then apply changes based on the patterns rather than any single run.
Capture general impressions after each run and apply them as broad prompt rewrites, since broad rewrites cover more potential issues than targeted changes.
Capture specific feedback after each run, translate it into targeted prompt or workflow changes, and observe whether subsequent runs improve.
Capture feedback as an aggregate quality score per run, since aggregate scores show whether quality is improving without requiring detail on individual issues.

questions.question: You are an operations assistant asking Claude to summarize 200 weekly metric records across multiple regions. Which output format communicates the data most clearly?

options.text: a structured table with one record per row and one metric per column, sorted by region
a bulleted list of observations grouped by region without consistent metrics across entries
a series of regional narrative briefs, each describing weekly performance in paragraph form
a narrative summary organized by region, describing trends and notable records in prose

questions.question: An analyst has been asked to compute summary statistics from an uploaded sales data file and produce a chart for a weekly report. Which output approach best fits the task?

options.text: Produce a written placeholder for the chart in the chat response without generating the actual visualization, leaving the weekly report without the visual output it requires.
Ask Claude to estimate the summary statistics from a brief preview of the file, accepting unverified figures rather than running the calculations against the full uploaded dataset.
Use Code Execution to perform the calculations and generate the chart, then verify the computed results against the source data before sharing the output.
Request a narrative description of the data in the chat response without computing values, leaving the summary statistics and the chart unproduced and the weekly report incomplete.

questions.question: An operations assistant is using Claude to support process optimization for an existing intake workflow. The assistant has access to the current process documentation and recent cycle-time data. Which activity best uses Claude to support this process optimization task?

options.text: Generate an optimized version of the intake process based on industry benchmarks, then compare it to the current process to identify gaps.
Use Claude to interview each team member who works on the intake process and synthesize the interview output into a redesigned workflow.
Map the current intake process, identify likely bottlenecks based on the cycle-time data, and propose optimization options for human review.
Apply Claude to predict the cycle- time impact of each proposed change and rank them so the team can implement improvements in priority order.

questions.question: A knowledge worker is explaining the purpose of an organizational Al governance tramework to a colleague. Which description is most accurate?

options.text: A governance framework lists the Al tools the organization licenses and the cost of each, so users can pick the most cost-effective tool for each task.
A governance framework defines the training every employee must complete before using Al tools, with separate equirements for each tool the organization licenses.
A governance framework documents the Al policies the organization is legally required to adopt, focusing on regulatory compliance rather than day-to- day use.
A governance framework defines approved tools, allowed data, required reviews, and reporting paths so Al is used consistently and accountably.

questions.question: You are organizing connected data sources for a team and must complete the planning steps before authorizingany connection. Which two planning steps must be completed BEFORE authorizing a new Connector? (Select two.) Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.text: Confirm the data classification of the source and the team's permission to use it.
Migrate every existing report off the prior data source onto the new Connector.
Confirm the Connector is on the approved-vendor list maintained by IT.
Decommission any unused legacy Connectors that may still be authorized.
Train every team member on the new Connector through formal training sessions.

questions.question: An HR associate is preparing to use Claude on a sensitive personnel matter. The organization's Al policy explicitly states that information related to ongoing investigations must not be entered into Al tools. Which response best aligns with the policy?

options.text: Refrain from entering investigation-related information into Claude and consult HR leadership for an approved alternative way to handle the matter.
Enter the investigation-related information into Claude in an Incognito chat, since Incognito chats do not retain information and therefore fall outside the policy's intent.
Enter a paraphrased version of the investigation-related information that removes identifying details, since paraphrasing addresses the spirit of the policy.
Enter the investigation-related information into Claude only after the investigation closes, since the policy applies during the investigation period.

questions.question: You are an operations lead mapping production tasks to Claude model strengths to set realistic expectations. Which two production tasks fit Claude's strengths most clearly? (Select two.) Each correct answer presents a complete solution.

options.text: monitoring a live sensor data stream and flagging anomalies as they occur in real time
synthesizing a single executive summary across many long source documents
issuing a binding legal determination based solely on Claude's analysis of case documents
calculating the precise settlement value of a derivative contract using live market inputs
drafting a tone-and-audience- aware customer-facing email under human review

questions.question: You are configuring a new Claude Project for a specific recurring workload Which Project configuration step should be performed first?

options.text: Add reference materials and instructions that the Project will rely on.
Invite collaborators to the Project and confirm the appropriate access levels.
Define the purpose of the Project and the recurring tasks it must support.
Test the configured Project on a representative request from the workload.

questions.question: You are a knowledge worker who decomposed a "draft a board memo" request into fifteen tiny steps and noticed the output now feels disjointed because related ideas were split apart. Which adjustment is most appropriate?

options.text: Remove all sequencing so the steps run in random order.
Combine the original request back into one unstructured sentence.
Subdivide each tiny step into ten more tiny steps for additional precision.
Consolidate related steps into fewer cohesive sections that group naturally connected ideas.

questions.question: A knowledge worker often switches between Claude and another Al service while working on a long-running project. Which Claude feature most directly reduces repetitive context-setting between sessions?

options.text: Open every Claude session in Incognito mode, which prevents the conversation from contributing to Memory and therefore eliminates the cross- session continuity the project would benefit from.
Rely on a single static Artifact pasted into each chat as the only continuity mechanism, ignoring the Memory feature that is purpose-built for retaining work- relevant context across sessions.
Disable Memory entirely and re- paste the same context paragraphs at the start of every Claude session, even though Memory is designed to retain that context across conversations automatically.
Enable Memory and use the import capability to bring relevant context from the other Al service into Claude as a starting point for the project's work.

questions.question: You are a project lead reviewing a teammate's habit of using the same prompt template for every task regardless of type. Which feedback is most warranted?

options.text: Task type has no effect on the appropriate prompting strategy.
The prompting strategy should not change between tasks because adapting it wastes time and adds no value.
The habit is ideal because a single template guarantees consistent quality across all task types.
The prompting strategy should be adapted to each task type because one template does not produce equally strong outputs across all tasks.

questions.question: You received a vague request to "look at our pricing." After discovery, the goal is confirmed: produce a structured competitor-pricing summary the team can act on, not new pricing ideas. Which strategy best fits the clarified task?

options.text: Use a divergent brainstorming approach to generate a wide range of possible competitor- pricing observations, then narrow to the most likely ones.
Use an open conversational strategy that explores competitor pricing iteratively across several prompts, allowing the structure to emerge from the conversation.
Use a comparative analysis strategy that contrasts the company's pricing against a single named competitor, since pairwise comparison produces the clearest output.
Use a research strategy that gathers structured information about competitor pricing, names sources, and notes confidence in each finding.

questions.question: You are an HR specialist reviewing data items proposed for inclusion in a Claude prompt. Which two data items are appropriate to include in a Claude prompt for a routine task? (Select two.) Each correct answer presents a complete solution.

options.text: Accommodation request notes from an employee's HR file needed to draft a role-adjustment memo.
Employee identification numbers and hire dates for the team roster included to help Claude personalize onboarding communications.
A compensation-band summary that includes employee names and current salary figures for a specific team.
An anonymized summary of an HR policy that the model will rephrase.
A redacted job description that the model will adapt for a posting.

questions.question: You are a marketing manager using Claude to ideate concepts for a campaign and must complete the framing steps before generating concepts. Which two framing steps must be completed BEFORE asking Claude to generate concepts? (Select two.) Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.text: Define the goal of the campaign and its success metrics.
Define the brand voice and the audience the concepts will address.
Schedule the campaign launch and rollout dates with the agency.
Review the Claude-generated concepts and select the two strongest for further development.
Select a finalist concept and prepare it for stakeholder approval.

questions.question: You are a product designer using Claude in a solution-design exercise. Which solution-design step should be performed first when using Claude?

options.text: Generate candidate solution concepts using Claude across diverse styles.
Compare the candidate concepts against the constraints and select a finalist.
Articulate the problem the solution must address and the constraints in play.
Produce detailed mock-ups of the chosen solution for stakeholder review.

questions.question: You are a customer-success manager considering whether to escalate a Claude- generated response. Which factor most strongly raises the impact of the output and supports escalation before external use?

options.text: The response is an unchanged draft for a paying customer that includes a service-level commitment.
The response is a brief internal announcement about an upcoming team all-hands meeting.
The response is an internal draft summarizing the associate's notes from a customer call for their own reference.
The response is a casual rephrasing of an internal team status update.

questions.question: You are reviewing a Claude-generated report whose tone is confident throughout. Which question best separates plausibility from verification?

options.text: Does the response use varied sentence structure across sections?
Does the response cover the topic comprehensively based on its length and section count?
Does the response open with a clear, well-framed statement of the main finding?
Can each specific claim be traced to a credible source or to the supplied input material?

questions.question: A Claude associate is incorporating reviewer feedback that named two specific issues with a Claude-drafted brief. The rest of the brief was accepted as written. Which next step is most likely to produce a strong revision?

options.text: Address the two specific issues and add a third improvement the associate identified, since combining reviewer feedback with self-identified improvements is more efficient.
Address the two specific issues and also revise unrelated sections to maintain a consistent voice across the brief after the edits.
Rewrite the briet trom scratch incorporating the two specific issues, since starting tresh integrates the teedback more cleanly than targeted edits.
Address the two specific issues directly, leave unrelated parts unchanged, and document the changes for the next review.

questions.question: You are a communications manager validating a Claude-generated newsletter that includes a specific industry growth figure. The figure appears in three trade-press articles, but none of them link to the underlying study. Which validation step is correct?

options.text: Remove the source attribution and present the figure as common knowledge.
Locate the original study referenced by the trade-press articles and verify the figure in the primary source.
Accept the figure because three trade-press articles repeat it.
Use the highest figure across the three articles to make the newsletter more compelling.

questions.question: You are a process consultant integrating Claude into an existing weekly workflow. Which is the correct order of integration steps? 1. Pilot the integrated workflow with a small group and gather feedback. 2. Document the current workflow steps, owners, and decision points. 3. Update the documented workflow and roll it out to the broader team. 4. Identify the steps where Claude can augment work and where humans must remain. 5. Define the inputs Claude needs, the outputs Claude returns, and the hand-offs around each step.

You are an operations assistant selecting a model for a recurring meeting-summary task that does not require deep reasoning and runs at moderate volume. Which selection best balances cost, speed, and quality?

options.text: A custom model, which the Associate-level user would need to build and train independently.
Opus, which prioritizes depth at higher latency and rate-limit consumption.
Sonnet, which provides solid quality at moderate latency and rate-limit consumption for everyday work.
Haiku, which is suitable only when the task requires the fastest possible turnaround.

questions.question: An HR business partner is configuring two separate Projects for two distinct client engagements. Which configuration best prevents context bleed between the two engagements?

options.text: Configure both Projects to share the same memory context to reduce setup effort, even though shared memory between unrelated client engagements is precisely the configuration that produces context bleed.
Set up each Project with its own distinct memory context, knowledge sources, and instructions, and verify that information from one Project does not appear in the other Project's responses.

Use a single shared Project for both client engagements with combined memory, knowledge sources, and tructions, on the assumption that Claude will keep the two clients' contexts separate without configuration.
Skip Project configuration entirely and use general chats for both engagements, which provides no scoped nemory contexts and offers no structural separation between the two clients' work streams.

questions.question: You are reviewing a Claude-generated competitor brief for unsupported claims. Which is the correct order of review steps? 1. Cross-check each specific claim against the supplied source material or trusted external references. 2. Decide whether to correct, re-prompt, or escalate based on the findings. 3. Document each unsupported or inconsistent claim with its location and severity. 4. Identify the specific factual claims, statistics, and citations in the brief. 5. Read the brief from beginning to end and flag any claims that feel surprising.

A business analyst has been asked to use Claude to extract requirements from a recorded stakeholder interview transcript. The transcript is approximately 90 minutes long and covers multiple topics. Which approach is most likely to produce a usable structured output?

options.text: Provide the transcript and ask Claude to produce a single ranked list of requirements, since a single list is easier for stakeholders to review than separate sections.
Provide the transcript and ask Claude to summarize it; extract requirements from the summary in a second pass since two passes catch more detail.
Provide the transcript and ask Claude to produce a chronological list of every statement that contains a verb, then classify each statement as a requirement or not.
Provide the transcript along with a structured prompt that requests must-haves, nice-to-haves, open questions, and conflicts as separate sections.

questions.question: A senior manager is reviewing a colleague's habit of never updating their team's Project configurations because "if it works once, it works forever.' " Which feedback is most warranted?

options.text: Configurations should be left alone if the team is satisfied with current outputs, and any required updates should be handled at the chat level rather than the Project level.
Configurations should be reviewed and updated periodically because policies, terminology, and source documents change over time, even when output quality has not visibly degraded.
Configurations should be updated on a fixed schedule regardless of whether the underlying policies and source documents have changed, since regular maintenance prevents drift.
Configurations should be updated only when output quality visibly degrades, since proactive updates risk introducing regressions in working configurations.

questions.question: You are an analyst reviewing a Claude response that addresses two of three required questions and skips the third. Which prompt element most likely needs strengthening?

options.text: The task statement should explicitly enumerate the three required questions and require an answer to each.
The output format should be revised to allow Claude to determine the appropriate structure for each question's answer.
The context provided to Claude should be expanded with additional background detail about the subject matter.
The role assigned to Claude should be changed to a more specialized expert persona to increase response depth.

questions.question: You are a Claude associate troubleshooting a recurring poor output. Which is the correct order of diagnostic steps? (1) Form a hypothesis about which prompt element most likely caused the deficiency. (2) Apply a single targeted change and observe the effect on the output. (3) Read the output end to end and identify the specific deficiency. (4) Compare the deficient output to the prompt to spot mismatches between input and output. (5) Document the root cause and the resolution for future reference.

A finance consultant is adapting a Claude- generated narrative for a quarterly investor update. Investors have a fixed time window for the call and expect the headline result and forward outlook to be clear early. Which adaptation is most appropriate for this audience?

options.text: Lead with the quarter's operational highlights, present the financial result in the middle for context, and close with the forward outlook.
Lead with a chronological recap of the quarter's events, present the headline result at the natural end of the recap, and conclude with the forward outlook.
Lead with the forward outlook, since investors are most interested in what comes next, and present the headline result and drivers afterward.
Lead with the headline result, present the key drivers concisely, and close with the forward outlook.

questions.question: You are a bank manager presented with a request to use Claude as the sole decision- maker on customer credit- line approvals. Which response is most appropriate?

options.text: Expand the design so Claude both evaluates applications and issues final approval notices to customers directly.
Accept the sole-decision-maker design because Claude can process applications faster than a human review team.
Decline the sole-decision-maker design and propose Claude assisting analysts who retain decision authority.
Implement the design on a pilot basis and notify compliance only if issues arise during production use.

questions.question: You are a research associate preparing inputs for a long task that references two lengthy regulatory documents, but only specific sections apply. Which approach best preserves context- window capacity?

options.text: Extract only the relevant sections from each document and include those, omitting unrelated chapters.
Skip the documents entirely and rely on Claude to invent the missing context.
Paste the full text of both documents without trimming to maximize the available material.
Split each document into one- character pieces and provide them one at a time.

questions.question: A finance manager must select a Claude feature for a task that requires deterministic calculations across a multi- tab spreadsheet. Which selection best fits the requirement?

options.text: Use the Research feature for the calculations, which gathers and synthesizes external sources and is not the appropriate feature for deterministic computation on an uploaded spreadsheet.
Use an Artifact alone for the calculations, which provides a stable editable surface for the result but does not perform the deterministic computation that Code Execution would run.
Use Code Execution, which runs code in a sandbox to perform calculations on the uploaded file and produce outputs the associate can verify.
Use a standard chat prompt for the calculations, which generates text without running code and does not produce the reproducible computational output the multi-tab calculation task requires.

questions.question: You are a business analyst evaluating a Claude-generated business case against the agreed acceptance criteria. Which is the correct order of evaluation steps? (1) Compare the business case with the source data and required topics. (2) Document gaps and inaccuracies for follow-up or correction. (3) Restate the acceptance criteria for the business case. (4) Decide whether to use the business case, iterate, or escalate. (5) Read the business case from beginning to end to form an initial impression.

An support representative is configuring a Project for drafting customer-facing apology emails after service outages. The current custom instructions tell Claude to "be empathetic and casual, keep it short, and offer a goodwill credit." The customer-service team has flagged that recent drafts have been too brief, have offered goodwill credits in cases where policy does not allow them, and have used contractions that the brand voice guide prohibits. Which adjustment best aligns the configuration to the use case?

options.text: Replace "be empathetic and casual" with "match the brand voice guide," remove the instruction to offer goodwill credits, and let each draft determine its own length based on the incident.
Keep the existing instructions and add a sentence telling Claude to consult the brand voice guide and the goodwill-credit policy that are attached to the Project knowledge base.

Move the brand voice guide and the goodwill-credit policy into the Project knowledge base and rely on the documents alone to govern tone, length, and credit decisions, without changing the custom instructions.

Specify the brand voice attributes (empathetic, formal, no contractions), set a minimum length, and instruct Claude to recommend a goodwill credit only when the attached eligibility policy permits one.

questions.question: You are a refining a prompt over several iterations. The output drifts further from the requested template with each change. Which step is most appropriate?

options.text: Continue making large simultaneous changes until the output happens to align.
Discard all prior versions and start with no record of what worked.
Revert to the version of the prompt that produced the closest match and adjust from that baseline.
Stop iterating and accept the most off-target version.

questions.question: You are a communications specialist preparing to describe Claude's role in a workflow to multiple stakeholder groups and must complete the preparation steps before drafting messages. Which two preparation steps must be completed BEFORE drafting the stakeholder messages? (Select two.) Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.text: Identify the stakeholder groups and what each group needs to understand.
Archive the drafted messages in the corporate communications repository.
Define the key facts about Claude's role and the boundaries that apply.
Schedule a follow-up forum to handle questions raised by the messages.
Send the drafted messages out and gather feedback for revision.

questions.question: You are a marketing manager using Claude to research a new market segment. Which research step should be performed first?

options.text: Validate the gathered information against authoritative external sources.
Define the specific research questions that must be answered for the segment.
Generate a final research report combining every Claude output produced.
Submit a series of Claude prompts to gather information across the segment.

questions.question: A Claude associate is identifying the bottleneck in a content workflow that takes too long to publish. The workflow has five steps: research, drafting, internal review, legal review, and publication. There is cycle-time data for each step from the past month. Which signal most directly identifies the bottleneck?

options.text: The step most recently added to the workflow, based on the assumption that process changes introduce the most friction.
The step where individual contributors report the highest workload in their weekly status updates.
The step with the highest average cycle time per item across the past month's runs.
The step with the longest queue or the largest backlog of items waiting to enter it.

questions.question: You are a knowledge worker summarizing common prompt failure patterns for the team. Which battern most often produces vadue or off-taraet outout?

options.text: A prompt that includes a representative example of the desired output.
A prompt that names a topic but does not state the task, audience, or required output structure.
A prompt that explicitly names the role, task, audience, and required output format.
A prompt that adds clear constraints on length and tone.

questions.question: A project lead is evaluating a Claude- generated status report against the project charter. The report will be delivered to a steering committee, which expects accurate status against committed milestones. Which set of criteria provides the strongest evaluation frame?

options.text: Readability, narrative flow, and whether the report tells a coherent story about the project's progress.
Length, formatting consistency, and tone appropriateness for a steering committee audience.
Accuracy of facts against the charter, completeness against required reporting fields, and relevance to the audience receiving the report.
Speed of generation, visual presentation quality, and consistency with the formatting used in previous status reports.

questions.question: You are a project manager weighing workflow steps by how much leverage Claude integration provides. Which workflow step typically offers the greatest Claude leverage in a knowledge-work team?

options.text: negotiating contractual terms with external parties on behalf of the company
drafting and synthesizing across many sources for a downstream reviewer
approving final deliverables for external publication without further review
making final personnel decisions about hiring, promotion, or termination

questions.question: You are an operations lead and notice that a Project's outputs have been drifting from the team's current expectations. Which maintenance action should be tried first?

options.text: Review the Project's instructions and reference materials against current standards.
Retire the Project and rebuild a new one from scratch with fresh content.
Switch the Project to a different Claude model in the hope it behaves better.
Continue using the Project and accept the drift as the new baseline of behavior.

questions.question: You are a customer-success lead running an interactive workflow where each turn must respond quickly and the per-turn reasoning is light. Which selection best aligns with the requirements?

options.text: Choose Haiku to keep latency low and to handle a light reasoning load efficiently at scale.
Choose any model because latency does not vary by model.
Choose a model based on the alphabetical order of its name.
Choose Opus to maximize reasoning depth despite higher latency.

questions.question: You are sorting Claude output structural defects by which most undermines clarity. Which structural defect most severely undermines the clarity of the output?

options.text: The main conclusion contradicts the evidence presented in the body.
Typographic inconsistencies appear throughout multiple sections of the document.
A single subheading is shorter than the other subheadings in the document.
Two adjacent paragraphs present the same information using inconsistent terminology.

questions.question: You are reviewing items proposed for inclusion in a Project that supports policy summaries. Which two items are appropriate to include in the Project? (Select two.) Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.text: the current policy library that the summaries are drawn from
presentation slides from a recent team training session on internal communication standards
active client case files maintained by a separate legal team for a different workstream
employee onboarding records used in a separate HR workflow managed by the same team
the summary format and the audience expectations the summaries must meet

questions.question: A manager is deciding what changes to make while conducting a Memory maintenance review for a long-running workflow. Which two actions best support Memory quality over time? (Select two.)

options.text: Delete all memories as the maintenance action to ensure a clean slate, then allow Claude to rebuild context organically through subsequent workflow runs.
Export the current memories as a backup before making changes, so prior context can be restored if a maintenance edit unintentionally removes information the workflow still depends on.
Identify and edit or delete entries that are stale, inaccurate, or no longer relevant, and add context Claude has not utomatically captured but the workflow continues to need.
Disable Memory entirely to eliminate the risk of stale entries surfacing in future workflow runs.
Leave all memories untouched on the basis that the workflow has been running consistently and no output- quality issues have been reported.

questions.question: You are a content creator. A first response from Claude is accurate but uses inconsistent terminology that does not match your organization's glossary. Which iterative change addresses the issue most directly?

options.text: Increase the requested length so the inconsistent terminology appears more often.
Remove the topic from the prompt to avoid the terminology issue entirely.
Provide the organization's glossary and instruct Claude to use only those terms throughout the response.
Ask Claude to invent additional terms unrelated to the glossary.

questions.question: Before sharing a Claude-generated brief, an analyst is applying the Al Fluency Framework Discernment competency to evaluate it. Which review best reflects Discernment principles?

options.text: Accept the brief on the basis that it reads fluently and the subject matter aligns with the analyst's professional knowledge of the topic.
Conduct a systematic check of the brief against the task requirements, source material, and professional standards before sharing it.
Review the opening paragraph and the conclusion of the brief, since these sections typically reflect the quality of the full document.
Skip the source material check during review and rely on overall tone and logical flow as proxies for factual accuracy.

questions.question: An associate is responding to an executive who claims that Claude will eliminate the need for any human review on customer-facing content. The executive is the budget approver for the team's Al tools. Which response is most appropriate?

options.text: Defer to the executive's authority and remove the human review step from customer-facing content, monitoring the results closely for the first several weeks.
Escalate the executive's claim to a senior leader outside the team before responding directly, since the issue affects more than just the associate's team.
Acknowledge the productivity gains, then explain that human review remains essential on customer-facing content because of accuracy and brand risk, with specific examples.
Pilot the executive's proposal on a low-risk subset of customer- facing content first, and use the pilot resultsto make the case for retaining human review on higher- risk content.

questions.question: You are evaluating a Claude output that appears to contain hallucinated content. Which response step should be performed first when a hallucination is suspected?

options.text: Notify the user community that the output contains a hallucinated claim.
Pinpoint the specific claim that appears to be unsupported by available evidence.
Discard the entire output and regenerate the output with a fresh prompt.
Document the hallucination pattern in the team's risk register for future reference.

questions.question: You are a project manager reviewing Claude usage approaches that teammates have proposed for a project workflow. Which two workflow steps are well-suited for Claude support? (Select two.) Each correct answer presents a complete solution.

options.text: deciding promotion outcomes for staff based solely on the model's judgment
drafting a structured project status update from a set of meeting notes
issuing legally binding contractual commitments on behalf of the company
synthesizing a literature review across many uploaded research documents
approving a final external press release without any human review

questions.question: You are using Claude to redesign an employee onboarding workflow and must complete the high-level decomposition steps before specifying detailed artifacts. Which two decomposition steps must be completed BEFORE specifying exact email content and the schedule? (Select two.) Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.text: Define the overall objective of the onboarding experience.
Negotiate the onboarding budget with the finance department.
Roll out the onboarding workflow to every new hire across the company.
Pilot the onboarding workflow with a small cohort of new hires.
Identify the major phases of the onboarding experience.

questions.question: You are optimizing a recurring Claude workflow and must complete the diagnostic steps before changing the worktlow. Which two diagnostic steps must be completed BEFORE changing the recurring workflow? (Select two.) Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.text: Identify the steps that contribute most to time, cost, or quality issues.
Deploy the updated workflow across the team and monitor for adoption issues.
Document the revised workflow steps and update the team's standard operating procedures.
Measure the current workflow's quality, time, and cost across recent runs.
Notify executive leadership of the projected savings from the optimization.

questions.question: You are a project manager reviewing stakeholder messages that teammates have drafted about Claude's role in a workflow. Which two messages are appropriate for stakeholder communication about Claude? (Select two.) Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.text: A claim that Claude will handle every task without any human involvement
A claim that the model never makes errors and requires no quality review
A vague reassurance that "the Al is taking care of it" without further detail
An honest description of where Claude assists and where humans retain decisions
A clear statement of the limits and known failure modes of the integration

questions.question: A learning specialist is configuring a Claude Project for a recurring course-design workflow. Which configuration approach best leverages a Skill alongside other Project elements?

options.text: Configure the Project with custom instructions that contradict the Skill's documented purpose, creating ambiguity about which guidance Claude should follow within the recurring course- design workflow.
Add the Skill to the Project but omit the supporting knowledge sources and any custom instructions, so the Project lacks the reference content and persistent guidance the workflow requires.
Upload the supporting knowledge sources but disable the relevant Skill, eliminating the packaged capability the workflow needs and forcing each chat to reconstruct the procedure manually.
Add the relevant Skill to the Project, upload the supporting knowledge sources, and write custom instructionsthat reterence both the Skill and the knowledge.

questions.question: A customer-success team member is reviewing a Claude-generated customer health-check report against the agreed deliverable list. The report covers all five required topics, but the renewal-risk section names only one risk factor where the deliverable specification calls for renewal risk to be assessed across pricing, product fit, and stakeholder change. Which conclusion is best supported?

options.text: The report meets the deliverable specification because all five required topics appear and the renewal- risk section is present in the output.
The report's completeness cannot be assessed from the deliverable specification alone; the customer should review the output and confirm whether the renewal-risk depth is sufficient.
The report meets the topic-level requirements but the renewal-risk section is under-scoped against the specification and should be expanded before delivery.
The report does not meet the deliverable specification because a section that addresses only one of three required risk dimensions counts as a missing section.

questions.question: An operations assistant is redesigning a recurring data-processing workflow step to use Code Execution. Which two design choices best support reliable integration? (Select two.)

options.text: Embed the Code Execution step inside the workflow without documenting the expected output format or the fields it produces.
Vary the input file format from run to run to accommodate the different source systems that supply the data each week.
Define a brief output-verification step in which a human reviewer confirms the computed result against an expected range or sanity check before the output advances to downstream consumers.
Standardize the input file format the step expects, so each Code Execution run receives consistent input and produces comparable, verifiable output across recurring weekly cycles.

questions.question: A senior project coordinator has been asked to use Claude to produce an end-of-year report covering finance, operations, and customer outcomes.
