options.text: Draft the three sections in parallel, each using a section-specific prompt, then concatenate and lightly edit the outputs into the final report.
Draft the executive summary first to anchor the report's narrative, then draft each section so it supports the summary already written.
Prompt Claude once with all source documents and request the full report, including the executive summary, in a single pass.
Define the report goals, gather inputs per section, draft each section in its own prompt, then synthesize the executive summary from the drafted sections.

questions.question: You are handling a document containing mixed-sensitivity content before using it with Claude. Which data-handling step should be performed first?

options.text: Submit the redacted document to Claude for the intended task.
Redact sensitive fields and replace them with appropriate placeholders.
Review the redacted document with a peer to confirm the redaction is complete.
Classify the content of the document and identify which fields are sensitive.

questions.question: A communications manager is drafting a prompt for Claude to produce a quarterly newsletter for store managers in three regions. The agreed key messages, regional details, and a prior newsletter the team liked are all available. Which prompt approach is most likely to produce a usable first draft?

options.text: Attach the prior newsletter and the agreed key messages, and ask Claude to produce a similar newsletter for this quarter.
Attach the prior newsletter, and ask Claude to match its tone and structure while incorporating the new key messages for the three named regions.
Name the audience, the three regions, the length, the tone, and the agreed key messages, and reference the prior newsletter only as a tone example.
Provide the agreed key messages and the three regions, and ask Claude to choose an appropriate length and tone for store managers.

questions.question: You are reviewing Connector setups that colleagues have proposed for various tasks. Which two Connector setups represent safe and appropriate uses? (Choose two.) Each correct answer presents a complete solution.

options.text: a Connector that links to the team's project management workspace under approved scope
a Connector that links to a personal cloud storage account where team member’s store working drafts alongside personal files
a read-only Connector that links to the public knowledge base for reference content
a Connector that links to the payroll system to allow team members to submit expense reports directly
a Connector that links to the personnel-records system for team leads to support scheduling tasks

questions.question: A knowledge worker is iterating a prompt that has produced a partly acceptable response. Which refinement practice produces the strongest learning across iterations?

options.text: Make several related changes in one iteration when they target the same weakness, and revert the whole set if the combined change makes the output worse.
Restart from a fresh prompt each iteration so that prior wording does not bias the next attempt, and pick the strongest response at the end.
Address every weakness the response showed in a single revision, then compare the revised output against the prior version.
Change one identifiable element per iteration, capture the change and its effect, and adjust another element only after the first is settled.

questions.question: An HR team member is reviewing a Claude- drafted set of interview questions intended for use across all candidates for a single role. The questions will be asked in the same order to every candidate. Which review practice best supports fairness?

options.text: Review the questions for length and tone, since the questions Claude drafts are well-aligned to role requirements by default and need only stylistic adjustment.
Review the questions and rotate the order across candidates so no candidate is consistently asked the hardest questions first.
Review the questions and add follow-up questions tailored to each candidate’s resume so each interview can explore the candidate’s specific experience.
Review the questions to ensure they apply equally to all candidates, avoid assumptions about candidate backgrounds, and focus on the role’s actual requirements.

questions.question: A Claude associate is troubleshooting a Claude response that addressed only one of three required questions in a prompt. The prompt listed all three questions in a single paragraph separated by commas. Which root cause is most likely?

options.text: The prompt’s audience and tone specification overshadowed the task statement, so Claude prioritized voice over coverage.
The prompt was too long and Claude focused on the question with the strongest grounding in the surrounding context.
The prompt’s task statement did not enumerate the three required questions explicitly enough for Claude to address each one in turn.
The prompt’s required questions were addressed implicitly across the response, even though the response did not visibly answer each question.

questions.question: You are evaluating whether a "redesign new- hire onboarding" request should be decomposed before prompting Claude. Which feature of the request most strongly indicates decomposition will help?

options.text: The request involves content the associate has produced many times before and knows can be handled in a single well- structured prompt.
The request involves a single well-defined output with a clear input and a familiar format.
The request requires multiple distinct outputs: a process map, supporting materials, and a measurement plan.
The request is for a single structured document that can be produced from one set of inputs in one prompt.

questions.question: A sales manager is iterating on a Claude- generated solution prototype after a stakeholder review identified two specific concerns. The rest of the prototype was accepted as written. Which iteration approach is most likely to produce a strong next version?

options.text: Rewrite the prototype from scratch incorporating the two specific concerns, since starting fresh integrates the feedback more cleanly than targeted edits.
Address the two specific concerns and also revise unrelated sections to maintain consistent voice across the prototype after the edits.
Address the two specific concerns and add a third improvement the associate identified, since combining stakeholder feedback with self- identified improvements is more efficient.
Address the two specific concerns directly, leave unrelated parts unchanged, and document the changes for the next review.

questions.question: You are an analyst fact-checking a Claude- generated report. Two cited sources give conflicting dates for the same event. Which approach is correct?

options.text: Average the two conflicting dates and use the average.
Locate a primary or authoritative source for the event and use the date that source confirms.
Choose the more recent date on the basis that later sources typically reflect updated or corrected information.
Publish both dates without resolving the conflict and let the reader choose.

questions.question: You are a senior analyst using Claude to analyze requirements from several stakeholder sources. Which is the correct order of steps? (1) Group related requirements and flag conflicts or ambiguities for stakeholder review. (2) Validate the structured output against the original sources for accuracy and completeness. (3) Submit the consolidated inputs to Claude with a structured extraction prompt. (4) Gather and label the source materials so each requirement can be traced. (5) Document the final requirements set with source traceability and status.
A Claude associate is applying the AI Fluency Framework Diligence competency to ongoing Claude usage. Which practice best reflects Diligence in a governance context?

options.text: Apply organizational AI policies consistently as a sustained professional habit, identify gaps between actual usage and the policies, and take corrective action to close those gaps over time.
Apply organizational AI policies only in high-visibility situations where usage is likely to be observed or reviewed by others.
Defer all policy application to a centralized compliance team, treating individual usage as outside personal responsibility.
Apply organizational AI policies during onboarding as a foundational training step, document that each associate has reviewed them, and treat that record as evidence of ongoing compliance.

questions.question: You are a procurement associate decomposing a vendor-evaluation task. Which dependency ordering reflects sound sequencing?

options.text: Score vendors first and decide on the criteria afterward.
Rank vendors before any data is collected.
Define evaluation criteria first, gather vendor data against those criteria, then score and rank.
Skip criteria and ask Claude to produce a vendor recommendation from no inputs.

questions.question: After importing context from another AI platform into Claude's Memory, a knowledge worker notices that some imported details did not appear in subsequent responses. Which explanation is most accurate?

options.text: The import transfers every detail as a rule, and any missing content reflects a deliberate choice by Claude to omit the information rather than the documented experimental nature of imports.
Memory imports are experimental, and Claude might not successfully incorporate all imported content; missing details can be added manually through Settings > Capabilities as a fallback.
Imported memories are stored separately from regular memories and cannot be referenced in any chat, so missing details reflect an architectural separation rather than imperfect import incorporation.
Memory imports overwrite all prior memories on completion, so any details that appear missing must have been deleted by the import process rather than not incorporated during the import itself.

questions.question: You are decomposing a “build a customer journey map” request. Which is the correct order of decomposed steps? (1) Identify the touchpoints the customer encounters during each stage. (2) Define the persona and the journey scope to be mapped. (3) Capture pain points and opportunities at each touchpoint. (4) Synthesize the findings into the final journey-map artifact. (5) Identify the major stages the persona moves through.
A knowledge worker is applying the AI Fluency Framework Description competency while revising an underperforming prompt. Which revision best reflects Description principles?

options.text: Add length to the prompt by inserting filler text that does not specify task scope, output format, audience, or constraints, leaving the original specification gaps in the underperforming prompt unaddressed.
Specify the task scope, the required output format, the audience, and the relevant constraints with sufficient clarity that the prompt produces a useful, reliable output on the next run.

Remove the existing context from the prompt and submit only the bare task statement, eliminating the audience, format, and constraint information that Description principles call for in a clear specification.
Replace the specific instructions with generic phrasing that broadens the task scope, undoing the specification work that Description principles require for a reliable, useful output on the next run.

questions.question: You are validating evaluation criteria proposed for a Claude-generated business brief. Which three criteria are valid for evaluating a Claude-generated brief? (Choose three.) Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.text: consistency of the writing style with the organization’s established tone guidelines
presence of an executive summary section as a structural completeness check
total word count of the output relative to industry benchmarks for business briefs
alignment of the output with the requested format and length constraints
factual accuracy of the claims made against the supplied source material

questions.question: You are an operations team member preparing inputs to summarize customer feedback. The feedback file mixes public quotations with personal contact details. Which preparation approach is most appropriate?

options.text: Replace the feedback content with the personal contact details and ask Claude to invent the missing feedback.
Strip out the feedback content and submit only the personal contact details.
Extract only the feedback content needed for the summary, redact or anonymize personal contact details, and submit the trimmed input.
Submit the entire file unchanged so Claude has complete context.

questions.question: Production monitoring shows that follow-up queries like “summarize what we learned about market trends” consistently take 40+ seconds. Investigation reveals the coordinator spawns the synthesis subagent for each summarization request, passing 80K+ tokens of accumulated findings. The coordinator already has these findings in its context from orchestrating the research. What’s the most effective way to improve response time for these follow-up summaries?

options.text: Spawn the synthesis subagent with reduced context and have it request specific findings from the coordinator on-demand.
Pre-generate and cache summaries at multiple granularities whenever new findings accumulate.
Enable prompt caching on the synthesis subagent to reduce the overhead of repeatedly transferring the same research findings.
Have the coordinator handle straightforward summarization requests directly using its existing context, reserving subagent spawning for complex analysis.

questions.question: You are a knowledge worker transitioning from a long, drifting conversation into a fresh focused session. Which is the correct order of transition steps? (1) Begin a new chat and paste the summary as its starting context. (2) Summarize the goals, key decisions, and open questions from the long conversation. (3) Identify which references should persist beyond the current chat. (4) Move persistent references into a Project’s knowledge base or attach them as needed. (5) Confirm the new chat is on-task before continuing the work.

An HR business partner is building a long- running workspace where a team handbook, a leveling guide, and a policies-FAQ document will be referenced across many separate chats by several team members. Which Claude feature is designed for this use case?

options.text: Generate an Artifact containing the three documents, which gives the team an editable surface for the reference content that persists across chats.
Attach all three documents to each chat as needed, since per- chat attachments give the chat direct access to the documents without additional setup.
Create a Project, which provides a persistent workspace with its own knowledge base and custom instructions shared across chats and members.
Connect the team’s Google Drive folder where the three documents live, so the connector surfaces them inside each chat at the moment the chat needs them.

questions.question: A customer sends: “This is frustrating. I’ve explained my issue twice and nothing is being resolved. I want to talk to a real person NOW.” The agent has not yet called any tools to investigate their account. What should the agent do?

options.text: Immediately call escalate_to_human with the conversation history.
Acknowledge the frustration and ask one targeted question to understand the specific issue before escalating.
First call get_customer and lookup_order to gather account context, then escalate to a human agent.
Briefly explain what the agent can help with and offer to resolve the issue quickly, escalating only if the customer repeats their request.

questions.question: A business analyst is converting a sticky-note request from a stakeholder into a structured prompt for Claude. Which is the correct order of conversion steps? (1) Confirm the audience and the decision the response must support. (2) Submit the structured prompt to Claude. (3) Identify the underlying task hidden in the sticky-note language. (4) Specify the desired length, tone, and output format. (5) Add the supporting facts and constraints relevant to the task.

You are a business analyst reviewing prompt drafts written by teammates. Which two elements belong in a well-structured prompt for a business task? (Choose two.) Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.text: a comprehensive list of company products and services to provide the model with business context
relevant context such as the audience and the goal of the task
a friendly, conversational tone instruction to make responses feel more approachable
a short personal anecdote to make the prompt feel more conversational
a clear statement of the task that the model must perform

questions.question: A strategy manager is reviewing a Claude- generated recommendation to consolidate the company’s two regional warehouses into one. The recommendation cites three sources that estimate cost savings and one source confirming that consolidation is operationally feasible. Two of the source documents also contain estimates of one-time transition costs and a stakeholder concern about regional service levels, neither of which appears in the recommendation. Which concern is most warranted?

options.text: The recommendation is sound because every source it cites supports the consolidation conclusion.
The recommendation is acceptable for an initial round, but the missing material should be added in a separate appendix rather than reprompting the original output.
The recommendation reflects selective use of the source documents and should be re- prompted to address the transition costs and the service- level concern before it is used.
The recommendation should be rejected because it relies on only four sources, which is insufficient for a decision of this size.

questions.question: You are a marketing manager deciding what to include in custom instructions for a writing- focused Project. Which two items belong in the custom instructions? (Choose two.) Each correct answer presents a complete solution.

options.text: the preferred writing style of the marketing manager who will review all final deliverables
the standard structure and the length expectations for typical deliverables
the brand voice and the tonal expectations the writing must follow
a representative sample of past writing that reflects the team’s preferred style and structure
the prompt author’s preferred response length for internal messages unrelated to external deliverables

questions.question: You are an operations lead sorting proposed Claude use cases by whether they are acceptable for your team to pursue. Which two proposed use cases are acceptable for the team to pursue with Claude? (Choose two.) Each correct answer presents a complete solution.

options.text: summarizing performance review notes across a team to support a manager’s promotion decisions
synthesizing themes across approved customer feedback under aggregation rules
drafting a preliminary symptom summary to support a clinician’s diagnostic review
drafting an internal training summary from approved internal documentation
drafting a legal summary that an attorney will review and edit before sharing with a client

questions.question: You are an analyst working on a one-off complex problem that genuinely requires multi-step reasoning over an extended chain of thought. Which model is best suited to this work?

options.text: Haiku, because lightweight models are always preferred regardless of complexity.
Opus, because it is positioned as the most capable for advanced reasoning on complex specialized tasks.
Any model, because reasoning depth does not vary across the lineup.
A non-Anthropic model, because the Claude lineup has no option for complex reasoning.

questions.question: Before uploading a customer file for a Code Execution analysis, a customer-success associate at Noventra, Ltd. is reviewing the planned task. Which two practices best align with sound data handling? (Choose two.)

options.text: Skip the upload review entirely on the basis of urgency, even though the file might contain regulated fields that organizational policy requires the user to redact before any code execution.
Bypass the data classification policy because the task is internal, treating sandboxed processing as an exemption from the review the policy requires before sensitive data is uploaded.
Confirm that the planned Code Execution task aligns with the organization’s data classification policy and escalate to the appropriate contact if the data sensitivity exceeds approved use.
Review the file for sensitive, confidential, or regulated fields before upload, and remove or redact any fields that are not required for the planned Code Execution analysis.
Upload the full unredacted customer file without review, on the assumption that a sandboxed execution environment removes the need to apply the organization’s data classification policy.

questions.question: You are a knowledge worker evaluating which Claude feature matches each proposed use case. Which two feature-to-use-case matches are appropriate? (Select two.) Each correct answer presents a complete solution.

options.text: Web search invocation to retrieve the established formula for calculating compound interest.
Long-context summarization for drafting a reply to a single short customer email.
Tool use to invoke a calculator for rephrasing a product description in simpler language.
A calculator tool for complex, multi-step pricing
Long-context summarization for a quarterly report distilled from many sources.

questions.question: A marketing manager is preparing a constrained brainstorming task: produce ten campaign ideas, each tied to a stated audience segment and each fitting one of three defined budget bands. Which prompting approach fits the task?

options.text: Ask Claude for thirty ideas with the audience and budget constraints stated in the prompt, then keep the strongest ten so a wider initial pool produces stronger finalists.
Ask Claude for ten distinct ideas, stating the audience constraints in the prompt and leaving the budget unconstrained so creativity is not limited at the ideation stage.
Ask Claude for ten distinct ideas with the audience and budget constraints stated in the prompt, and require each idea to name which audience and budget band it addresses.
Ask Claude for ten distinct ideas without budget constraints, then filter the output afterward to keep only the ideas that fit the three budget bands.

questions.question: A learning specialist is configuring a Project for course-design work. Their organization has an internal instructional-design standard and a preferred output structure for lesson outlines. Which custom-instruction set best supports this use case?

options.text: Name Claude's role as a course designer, require alignment with the organization's instructional- design standards, and specify the preferred output structure for lesson outlines.
Specify only the preferred output structure for lesson outlines, since the structure carries the standards implicitly and naming the role adds no value.
Name Claude's role as a course designer and require alignment with the organization's instructional- design standards; leave the output structure to Claude based on each lesson's topic.
Name Claude's role as a course designer; let each chat prompt specify the standards and output structure for that lesson, since lessons vary widely.

questions.question: You are designing a checklist for evaluating Claude outputs and must complete the upstream steps before scoring an output. Which two steps must be completed BEFORE scoring a Claude output against the checklist? (Choose two.) Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.text: Specify the threshold that distinguishes acceptable from unacceptable output.
Promote the approved output into the downstream production process.
Define the evaluation criteria that matter for the task at hand.
Forward unacceptable outputs to a senior reviewer for second-pass review.
Document the final score and the reviewer comments for the audit trail.

questions.question: A knowledge worker notices that a Claude output may have repeated a confidential financial figure from an internal source that the user was told to treat as restricted. The output has not yet been shared outside the user. Which immediate action is most appropriate?

options.text: Continue using the output for the intended internal purpose, since the figure has not left the user's possession and no external disclosure has occurred.
Edit the output to remove the figure, save the edited version for the intended use, and document the change in a personal log without involving the governance channel.
Stop using the output, document the issue-including the prompt and the source-and report it through the documented governance or incident channel.
Stop using the output and start a new chat with a more carefully scoped prompt, since the issue is resolved as long as the original output is not used.

questions.question: A procurement manager is evaluating a Claude-generated vendor proposal summary against the original RFP. The RFP lists twelve numbered requirements across pricing, security, and service levels. How should the summary be checked for completeness?

options.text: Map each numbered requirement in the RFP to a section of the summary and confirm that every requirement is represented.
Spot-check three random requirements from the RFP against the summary, since random sampling is the standard completeness check for summaries.
Compare the section headings in the summary with the section headings in the RFP, since matching headings indicate matching content.
Read the summary end to end and confirm that it forms a coherent response to the RFP, since coherent summaries typically reflect coverage of the source.

questions.question: You are a product manager asking Claude to produce an interactive prototype of a small landing-page mockup that the team will iterate on and share. Which Claude feature is best suited to this output?

options.text: A new Project containing only the team's prior meeting notes.
An Artifact, which presents standalone editable content in a dedicated side panel for iteration.
A Research run that produces a multipage external survey of competitor sites.
A short conversational reply embedded inline in the chat history.

questions.question: You are an operations lead choosing actions when a Claude conversation has degraded in quality. Which recovery action should be tried first when conversation quality degrades?

options.text: Replace the model with a different vendor's model immediately.
Escalate to a senior architect for a manual review of the conversation history.
Discard the entire conversation and rebuild the work from the original prompt.
Summarize the current state and continue with a focused follow-up prompt.

questions.question: A knowledge worker is explaining context- window basics to a teammate. Which statement most accurately describes a context window?

options.text: The complete conversation history retained across sessions, which the model can reference whenever it produces a response in any chat.
A bounded amount of text the model can consider at once, including the conversation history, attached documents, and the current input.
The subset of the conversation that the model determines is most relevant to the current input, which can be smaller than the full conversation.
An adjustable setting that determines how much of the conversation history the model includes in each response, configurable per chat.

questions.question: A product manager is using Claude to ideate options for a new self-service portal. The team needs breadth before narrowing and will evaluate trade-offs across the options in a separate session. Which prompting strategy fits this stage?

options.text: Request multiple distinct options ordered by Claude's assessment of feasibility, so the team can focus its trade-off discussion on the most feasible options first.
Request a single recommended option with strong reasoning, since well-reasoned single options give the team a clearer starting point than several weakly reasoned alternatives.
Request multiple distinct options and ask Claude to recommend the strongest one with reasoning, so the team starts the trade-off discussion from a leading candidate.
Request multiple distinct options with stated trade-offs, and avoid committing to a single recommendation in this round.

questions.question: A prompt describes a multi-step setup process, such as configuring an environment and then running a script, but Claude sometimes performs the steps out of order. What change would make the required order unambiguous?

options.text: Provide the instructions as a numbered list of steps in the exact order they must run
Combine all of the steps into a single long sentence separated only by commas
Describe the steps in a random order and let Claude infer the correct sequence
Remove the step numbers and rely only on paragraph breaks to imply the correct order

questions.question: A marketing manager needs to draft a persuasive email campaign to launch a new product. The email should capture attention, highlight benefits, and include a call to action. Which prompting approach is best?

options.text: Instruct Claude to write a thorough product description report covering all features, specifications, technical details, and pricing info, formatted as a formal document that is suitable for internal stakeholders rather than a marketing audience.

Prompt Claude to draft an email announcing the new product, leaving the structure and content entirely to the model's discretion without providing any specific guidelines on audience, tone, or key product benefits to highlight.

Ask Claude to produce several email drafts with distinct tones (formal, casual, urgent), then assess each draft's persuasiveness, clarity, and brand alignment, and choose the best one for final edits, and then iterate if needed.

Guide Claude to create a marketing email: first, write an attention-grabbing subject line; then, open with a hook; next, present three key benefits with persuasive language; and finally, include a clear call to action linked to the product page.

questions.question: A business analyst is deciding whether to send one large request or break it into stages. Which two features of a request are the strongest signals that it should be decomposed? Select two.

options.text: It bundles several distinct deliverables that are meant for different audiences and uses.
It concerns a subject area the analyst has not personally worked in for several years.
Later parts are only worth producing if the earlier factual work is correct.
It runs to a long prompt because a good deal of background has been pasted in with it.
It asks for the final answer to be presented as a table rather than as flowing paragraphs.

questions.question: A support lead finds a Claude-drafted troubleshooting article accurate but written at a reading level too advanced for the average customer. Which follow-up instruction best refines the draft without sacrificing accuracy?

options.text: Remove the least common troubleshooting steps so the article reads a bit shorter
Add more technical detail so customers understand the underlying cause in full
Convert the article into a formal specification format used by the engineering team
Rewrite the article with shorter sentences and everyday words, keeping every step accurate

questions.question: A retention lead asked why cancellations rose sharply in the last quarter. The answer explains at length what cancellation rates are and how they are generally measured. How should she judge this output?

options.text: As adequate for now, because background on how the measure works is a reasonable place to begin the analysis.
As accurate but off target, because it explains the topic instead of addressing the rise she asked about.
As evidence that the question cannot be answered, since the reply avoided the specific rise she was asking about.
As a sound answer that simply needs shortening, since the explanation contains more detail than she required here.

questions.question: A Claude draft attributes a sentence to a named industry report as a direct quotation. What is the appropriate validation step?

options.text: Ask Claude for the page number, and accept the quotation once a number has been supplied to her.
Confirm that the report exists and was published, which establishes the quotation's origin.
Open the report and find that exact sentence, since a close paraphrase may not appear in it.
Search for the sentence's key phrase and accept it if similar wording appears anywhere.

questions.question: A manager needs a comparison of six suppliers across five criteria. The information is currently spread across several separate Claude answers. What should she do first?

options.text: Agree which suppliers and which criteria belong in the comparison before asking for any output.
Ask Claude to rank the six suppliers straight away and work backwards from the ranking it gives.
Ask Claude to combine all of the earlier answers into one long document she can read through.
Choose the output format now, so that every further answer can be produced in that same shape.

questions.question: A communications officer must publish a Claude-drafted market briefing on the company blog within the hour. Claude used web search to produce it, and every figure in the draft carries a citation. What is the appropriate first step before she publishes?

options.text: Ask Claude how confident it is in each figure, and revise the ones it rates as least confident.
Open the cited sources and confirm that each figure in the draft does appear in the page it points to.
Add a line at the foot of the briefing noting that it was prepared with the help of an AI assistant.
Regenerate the briefing in a fresh conversation, and publish if the two drafts report the same figures.

questions.question: A communications assistant receives an answer containing a clearly incorrect statement about her organisation. She corrects her own draft in a follow-up message, and also wants the problem itself recorded rather than just worked around. What should she do?

options.text: Use the thumbs-down control on the response that contained the incorrect statement, in addition to fixing her own draft.
Start the same task again in a new conversation, on the basis that a clean chat is less likely to repeat the mistake.
Rephrase her original prompt in more forceful language so that the incorrect statement is less likely to recur next time.
Add a line to the conversation noting that the earlier statement was wrong, so the correction sits in the chat history.

questions.question: A marketer is midway through a one-off brainstorm that will not be revisited, and the conversation is approaching its limit. What is the most appropriate action?

options.text: Build a Project and move the whole brainstorm into project knowledge before writing anything more.
Let the conversation continue and condense itself, since nothing in it needs to outlive this session.
Split the brainstorm across four separate chats so that no single conversation ever nears its limit.
Stop the brainstorm now and restart it in a new chat so the ideas come from a completely clean window.

questions.question: A market analyst must produce a competitor briefing drawn from many public sources, and the team will keep editing that briefing for weeks afterwards. Which two Claude features fit this job? Select two.

options.text: Keep the briefing inline in the chat and re-paste the newest version whenever an edit lands.
Ask for the briefing as an artifact, so the team can edit and reuse it outside the chat.
Turn on a mail connector first so that the competitor facts are drawn from the team inbox.
Use Research mode, so the briefing is built by multi-step searching and returns citations.
Open a separate chat for each competitor so that no single conversation ever grows long.

questions.question: A support operations lead must classify a large daily backlog of short inbound messages, and separately needs one deep analysis of a tangled contract dispute. Which two choices fit? Select two.

options.text: Use the fastest, cheapest tier for both jobs, since the tiers differ mainly in reply speed.
Use the deepest-reasoning tier for both of the jobs, since the strongest option is never bad.
Use the fastest, cheapest tier for the high-volume classification, where throughput matters.
Use the deepest-reasoning tier for the contract dispute, accepting the larger quota it uses.
Use whichever tier the team already has open, since the tier rarely changes what comes back.

questions.question: A new team member asks how the Claude model tiers actually differ from one another in everyday use. Which two statements are accurate? Select two.

options.text: Moving up one tier is the standard fix whenever a prompt comes back with a vague or shallow answer.
The lightest tier gives answers of the very same depth, only more slowly than the other two.
The deepest tier suits genuinely hard problems, and it consumes meaningfully more allowance.
The mid tier is the fast, capable default, and it is the right pick for most everyday work.
The tiers differ only in writing style, so any of them may be used for any task at any time.

questions.question: A team is setting up a new recurring weekly task and has to decide how much reasoning depth it needs. Which sequence is correct?

options.text: Run the task on several tiers at once, then write down what good output means, then compare the results against that definition, then keep the tier that did best.
Compare a sample of results with what colleagues produce by hand, then write down what good output means, then pick a tier on that basis, then run the task each week from then on.
Pick a tier by how important the task feels, then run it for a month, then write down what good output means, then compare the month's results against that.
Write down what good output means, then run a real sample on the default tier, then compare that sample against the definition, then change tier only where it falls short.

questions.question: A team runs two workloads that are alike in volume and subject matter. One is edited line by line by a specialist before use; the other is published automatically with no human reading it. Which consideration should weigh most heavily when choosing a tier for each?

options.text: How much a downstream human check would catch, since the unchecked workload has to carry its own quality with no safety net.
The subject matter the two workloads share, since comparable material should be handled the same way for consistency of output.
The volume of the two workloads, since equal volumes imply equal throughput needs and therefore the same balance of speed and cost.
The seniority of the people who own each workload, since the more senior owner is accountable for the more visible of the two.

questions.question: Reviewing a backlog of intake forms, an analyst notices that most entries name a solution rather than a need, for example "we need a dashboard." How can Claude best help with this backlog?

options.text: Ask Claude to restate each entry as the outcome sought, then flag entries where that outcome is unclear.
Ask Claude to group the entries by the department that submitted them and report the totals to sponsors.
Ask Claude to reject entries that name a tool and ask the submitters to resubmit them in the right form.
Ask Claude to design the dashboard described in each entry so submitters can confirm what they wanted.

questions.question: In a pilot of a new Claude-assisted briefing arrangement, three of eight testers report that the output is "not quite right" but say nothing more specific. What should the pilot's owner do first?

options.text: Pause the pilot until the owner can sit with each tester and watch a full briefing being produced.
Ask the three testers for specific examples, with what the output said and what it should have said.
